To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the K^+k^- S-wave contribution can be properly taken in account in the determination of 2beta_{s} and that the sign of cos(2beta_{s}) can be determined by using interference of K^+K^-, S and P-wave ampletudes.

(1) the presence of a K^+ K^--S wave component does not bias the measured value of the CP-violating phase 2 beta(s), (2) the statistical error on the determination of 2 beta(s) is increased by less than 20%, and (3) the strong phase between the S-wave and P- wave amplitudes is not determined by the B-factories and must be measured by the LHCb experiment

the presence of an S-wave in the K^+k^- final state in the B_s --> J/psi K_k^- decay has a small effect on the measurement of 2beta_{s}, and that the sign of cos(2beta_s) is accessible by measuring the strong phase between the S- and P-wave ampltudes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of 2beta_{s} in B0_{s} -> J/psiK^{+}K^{-} decays in the presence of a K^{+}K ^{-} S-wave component.
the measurement of the CP violating angle 2beta_s in B_s -> J/\psi K^+K^-.
the study of the decay B_s -> Jpsi K^+K^-, where K^+K^{-} is in a P-wave.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the S-wave contribution to the decay B_s -> J/Psi K^+K^-, while not negligible, is not a problem in determining the phase 2beta(s).
the presence of an S-wave in the final state is not a problem, and can be properly accounted for in the analysis.
, while the S-wave component is important and should be included in the fit, the effect on 2beta(s), including statistical and systematic errors, is not large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the S-wave component is not a serious problem for the determination of 2beta_S, and the sign ambiguity of cos2beta_S may be solved in the future.
we can determine 2beta_s to the same accuracy as if we were ignoring the K^+k^- S-wave contribution.
the effect of a K^+K^--wave contribution in B_s -> Jpsi K^+K- decays is not large enough to affect the determination of the phase 2beta(s).
The main takeaway from our work is that
if an S-wave component is observed in B0(s)-> J/psi K^{+}K^{-} decays, it is important to include it in the analysis of the CP violating phases.
the presence of the K^+k^- S-wave component can cause a bias in 2beta_s of the order of the statistical error on the measurement.
a measurement of cos2beta is feasible with the present B-factory data.
